problem: MLLMs used in embodied agents mostly do short-horizon reactive planning and fail to build global spatial representations from long egocentric video, so long-horizon spatial reasoning and planning degrade sharply. Existing spatial benchmarks use multiple-choice or numeric matching rather than physical verification.
motivation: Biological intelligence relies on 'mental navigation': building cognitive maps from experience and mentally simulating routes before acting. The paper asks whether MLLMs can do this from >5-minute egocentric videos, and builds a benchmark with simulator-verified plans to probe it.
key_idea: Define mental navigation (video -> hierarchical cognitive map -> landmark-grounded route plan, verified in Habitat) and train NavMind with cognitive maps as explicit intermediate representations via progressive SFT with perplexity-based rejection sampling (CogRS).
insight: Even with ground-truth cognitive maps, frontier MLLMs reach only about 11.8% SR_t on average (Table 2 vs Table 1), so the bottleneck is structured spatial reasoning rather than perception alone. Explicit map-then-plan supervision on Video2Mental lifts SR_p to 38.0% vs about 3.8% for baselines. Ablations (Fig. 3A, figure only) reportedly show that the hierarchical map beats flat grid maps and that CogRS helps most on medium and long tasks.
method: Task formulation: input is an egocentric video with poses plus a start/target query; output is a hierarchical cognitive map M and a landmark-grounded plan P (lm, semantic label, relation, bbox).
Video2Mental data: about 24k samples from 246 HM3D/MP3D Habitat scenes; random-tour egocentric videos at 640x480 with 360° scans; shortest-path plans; Short/Medium/Long difficulty levels.

Hierarchical cognitive map: Region -> Landmark -> Object; landmarks are chosen by footprint area, objects attach to the nearest landmark with (8-direction bearing, same/on, distance), and regions come from Gaussian-affinity spectral clustering.
Stage-1 SFT: Qwen3-VL-8B is fine-tuned on the full training set with a weighted NLL on the map plus the reasoning chain conditioned on the map.

CogRS: using the stage-1 model, compute perplexity on decision-critical tokens (landmark selection, spatial relations), keep samples in a moderate interval [tau_min, tau_max], and run stage-2 progressive SFT on more than 3,000 hard trajectories.
Dual evaluation: text-based metrics (Landmark IoU/F1, NE, NE_waypoint, SR_t with NE<1m) and Habitat pointnav execution-verified metrics (SR_p, SPL).
Downstream integration: NavMind acts as a planner and Uni-NaVid executes each landmark/relation step as the low-level VLN policy.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-8B (fully fine-tuned, two-stage SFT); Uni-NaVid as downstream executor
setting.training_data: Video2Mental training split (21,330 samples, HM3D/MP3D synthetic simulator videos); stage 2 uses over 3,000 filtered hard samples
setting.observation: long egocentric RGB video (>5 min, 640x480) with camera poses
setting.action_space: landmark-based plan (landmark, relation, bbox) converted to waypoints and executed by the Habitat pointnav; Uni-NaVid low-level actions in downstream use
setting.privileged: none for the main MN setting; the MN (w/ GT-Map) setting supplies the ground-truth cognitive map

numbers_note: The paper's own benchmark (Video2Mental) is the only one with tables. The seen/unseen split, ablation (Fig. 3A), MP3D unseen results (350 samples) and Uni-NaVid integration (20 scenes) are given only in figures, so no numbers are extracted. The Qwen3-VL-8B/30B baselines' Landmark IoU/F1 were not tabulated. Only the abstract, intro and experiments were available; the supplementary is template text.
results: NavMind-Stage2 gets SR_t 48.8 / SR_p 38.0 / SPL 35.2 / NE 2.92 on Video2Mental vs the best baseline Qwen3.5-397B (SR_t 10.7, SR_p 7.4, SPL 5.9). Baselines average SR_t 5.54% and SR_p 3.76%, and even with GT maps they only reach about 11.8% SR_t. Paired with Uni-NaVid, NavMind reached a target in 34 actions where Uni-NaVid alone failed after 274 (a single qualitative example).
limitations: The benchmark and training data are synthetic, from Habitat scenes with rule-based cognitive maps and shortest-path supervision; there is no real-world or real-video evaluation.
Downstream VLN gains and the ablations/generalization results are shown only in figures, and the VLN integration uses a 20-scene set with one policy (Uni-NaVid).
Success is defined as NE<1m via rule-converted waypoints, so it depends on the landmark-to-waypoint conversion, and the model is trained and evaluated on the same pipeline of generated data.
